picks.why: The Naoussa house founded in 1879, whose cellar carried the appellation's name abroad; the Grande Reserve, aged long in oak and bottle before release, is the old school Naoussa a sommelier is asked about.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the label form for the years taught (Naoussa Grande Reserve or Grande Reserve Naoussa) and its ageing before release from the house and a second source; name the founder only with his dates from two sources and no living member of the family. Its Goumenissa, Mantinia and Cretan wines go in others: one flagship a producer.

picks.why: Yianakohori estate founded in 1997 by a member of the Boutari family after he left the family firm; Ramnista is its Naoussa, Xinomavro in the structured, modern style.
picks.note: Kali Riza and Akakies, the house's Amyndeon wines, go in others, which is why the house is not an Amyndeon pick. Boutari and Kir-Yianni are separate companies of one family origin, as the library's trap says. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Trilofos estate farmed organically whose whole bunch, gently extracted Xinomavro changed how Naoussa is read; Earth and Sky, Gi kai Ouranos on the Greek label, is its old vine Naoussa.
picks.note: The library leaves founded empty; the first vintage of Earth and Sky is given as 2003 in one source and 2005 in another, so leave it out unless two agree. Confirm the two sites of the blend (Trilofos and Fytia by one account) and that the label carries Naoussa PDO. The Rapsani wine, made with the Liapis family under the Terra Olympus name by one account, goes in others. The lint's family word test may read the Earth of the name as bare: write Earth and Sky whole. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: One of the old family cellars of Naoussa town; Paliokalias, a single vineyard of Xinomavro south east of the town long tied to the family, shows the perfumed, old vine side of the district.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The family's tenure from 1840 comes from a retailer: confirm from the house and a second source or leave founded empty. Confirm the label form (Paliokalias, Naoussa PDO) and the site's altitude; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small family estate at Gastra above the town, whose first wines date from 1992 by one account; its Naoussa, from its own Xinomavro, is the appellation in the hands of a grower.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the first vintage of 1992 and the village of Gastra from two sources. The region record calls it a one wine grower, but a blend with Cabernet Sauvignon and Merlot is also reported: confirm before teaching it as one wine. Name no living member of the family.

picks.wine: Barba Yannis Reserve Vieilles Vignes Xinomavro
picks.why: Estate founded in 1997 at Agios Panteleimon on the Amyndeon plateau; its Reserve Vieilles Vignes comes from the Barba Yannis block, ungrafted Xinomavro planted in 1919 that phylloxera never reached.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The label has read Ecosystem Reserve Vieilles Vignes and later Barba Yannis Reserve Vieilles Vignes: teach the form of the years taught and confirm the planting of 1919 from the house and a second source. The Hedgehog single vineyard Xinomavro and the Amyndeon rosé go in others. Name no living founder.

picks.why: Organic estate with old Xinomavro in several villages of the plateau, known above all for traditional method sparkling wine; the Extra Cuvée de Réserve is its long aged sparkling Xinomavro, the appellation's sparkling face.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the exact label and its colour (a Cuvée Rosé is also made), whether it carries PDO Amyndeon or a regional PGI, its time on the lees and the founding year. Amyndeon and Zitsa are the two Greek appellations for sparkling wine by one source: confirm before saying so. Name no living founder.

picks.why: The growers' co-operative of the town, at work since 1959 by the Wines of Greece account and for decades the appellation's whole output; its rosé of Xinomavro is the style Amyndeon alone holds as a PDO among the grape's appellations.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. IN DOUBT: the label of the co-operative's rosé was not confirmed this run. The author confirms the wine and its exact name as printed, or the merge agent drops the pick. Confirm the house's own name (Agricultural Cooperative of Amyndeon, Coop. Amynteo) and 1959. Shares and volumes stay out.

picks.why: Family winery in the town of Goumenissa whose red of the appellation, Xinomavro and Negoska fermented together as the law asks, is the traditional reference for the district's blend.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the flagship's exact label (the house's Goumenissa PDO, or an old vine bottling if that is the one to know) and the founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Organic family estate at Goumenissa that works the appellation's blend and its grapes one by one; its Goumenissa is Xinomavro with Negoska in the classic form.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the organic certification and its year, the label's spelling (Chatzivaritis or Hatzivariti) and the founding year; varietal Negoska and Roditis go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Goumenissa family estate growing vines since 1924 by its own account, working with wild yeast, little sulphur, long maceration and no filtration; its Goumenissa carried the district onto natural wine lists abroad.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1924 from two sources, the label's exact name, and whether the wine carries PDO Goumenissa or a regional PGI (a natural producer may leave the appellation): if it does not carry the PDO, choose the house's PDO wine or swap the pick. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: An older Goumenissa winery taken over in 2018 by the founders of Ktima Biblia Chora and renamed; its Goumenissa is the classic blend of about four parts Xinomavro to one of Negoska.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the year of the takeover (2018 in one source), the name of the winery before it and its founding; name no living person of either family.

picks.why: The large Macedonian house that took up Rapsani in 1991 and replanted the Olympus terraces with the local growers, for years the appellation's only producer; its Reserve and Grande Reserve, the three grapes fermented together and aged in oak, carried Rapsani for a generation.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm which of the two is the flagship (Rapsani Reserve or Grande Reserve) and that it is released under that name; the ageing each term asks from the PDO's own text; the house's founding (1890 is commonly given) from two sources. Tell its work with the growers as history with its dates, nothing of the present.

picks.why: Family winery at the foot of Olympus in the Tempi valley, at Rapsani since 1991 by one account; its Rapsani Old Vines, Xinomavro, Krassato and Stavroto from the north east slopes, puts a grower's name beside the large house.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the year the winery came to Rapsani, the label form (Rapsani Old Vines, PDO Rapsani), the site's name (Prosilia by one account) and its altitude from the house; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Rapsani family who planted their first vineyard about 1935 by their own account and built a modern winery in the 2000s; its Rapsani is the village's own red, and the family works the vines of a Rapsani venture with Thymiopoulos by one account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house writes itself under a living man's name: a house keeps its name, but the prose names nobody. Confirm the plain Rapsani PDO label, about 1935 and the winery's date from two sources, and say how the Terra Olympus wines stand between the family and Thymiopoulos only as two sources agree.

picks.why: Argolid house of the 1980s with vineyards high in the Nemea hills; the Grande Cuvée, Agiorgitiko alone from red clay, first bottled in 1996 by the house's account, is its Nemea.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year (1986 is often given) and the house's village from two sources, the first bottling of 1996 and the vineyard's altitude from the house's technical sheet; Megas Oenos, the blend with Cabernet Sauvignon, goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate at Ancient Nemea, among the first in the district to bottle its own wine and to farm organically; Palaia Klimata, Old Vines on the export label, is Agiorgitiko from its oldest vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The house says it has worked Agiorgitiko since 1876: hedge it as the house's claim or leave founded empty. Confirm the label form for the years taught (Palaia Klimata in Greek, Old Vines abroad) and the oak regime; Mikroklima goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Nemea estate the Tselepos family of Mantinia founded in 2003 on old Agiorgitiko at Koutsi; the Reserve is its Nemea for the cellar, the family's red answer beside its Mantinia white.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The same family as the Mantinia pick Tselepos: a separate estate with its own name and wine, which the record says plainly. Confirm 2003, the vine age and the label's spelling (Driopi or Dryopi); Driopi Classic goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate at Petri founded in 1996 and dry farmed; Monopati, from Agiorgitiko vines more than fifty years old aged in barrique, is its old vine Nemea.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1996, Petri, the vine age and the barrel regime from the house and a second source; Le Sang de la Pierre, a cuvée in one listing, goes in others if confirmed. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate near Tripoli founded in 1989 and farmed organically; its Mantinia, Moschofilero from the high plateau, is the reference a sommelier is expected to know for the appellation.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. One source gives 1989 for the estate and another a settling in Mantinia in 1981: confirm from the house. Confirm the village (Rizes is often given) and the label form; Blanc de Gris and the sparkling Amalia go in others. Driopi, the family's Nemea estate, is the Nemea pick. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Long established family estate on the plateau, organic since 1993 by its own account; its Mantinia is the traditional, fresh face of Moschofilero.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. A founding of 1870 is claimed in one source and borne out by none: leave founded empty unless two agree. Confirm the organic year and the label form; Ode Panos, the sparkling Moschofilero, goes in others if confirmed. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Younger family winery on the plateau making Moschofilero in the modern, aromatic style; Holy Mania is its PDO Mantinia, while its Fteri is labelled as a regional wine of the Peloponnese.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm Holy Mania's PDO and the vineyard, the founding year, and Fteri's PGI; Fteri and Hoof & Lur go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family winery at Steno that makes Moschofilero alone and has bottled Mantinia since 2009; its Mantinia shows the appellation from one family's vines.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 2009 and the village of Steno from two sources and the founding year; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: House founded in 1979 at Stamata in Attica, with a winery at Koutsi in Nemea from 2003 and the old Nassiakos cellar in Mantinia; Mantinia Nassiakos, the Moschofilero of that cellar, is the house's flagship by a Greek trade account.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1979, Stamata, Koutsi in 2003 and the history of the Nassiakos cellar from two sources; the Nemea Reserve and Grande Reserve go in others, which is why the house is the Mantinia pick and not Nemea's. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family house of 1966 in the hills of Heraklion, which brought Plyto and Dafni back from near loss; its Plyto, the white of a grape almost gone, is the revival in one glass.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1966, the village and the year of the first Plyto from the house and a second source. Dafni and the old vine Liatiko of the Aggelis vineyard go in others; Dafni may be argued the flagship, so choose one with two sources. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family winery at Dafnes south of Heraklion, known for its work with Vidiano; Dafnios Vidiano is the island's revived white grape in the house's hand.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm that the white Dafnios is Vidiano, its appellation (PGI Crete or a PDO), and the founding year; the red Dafnios Liatiko and the sparkling Vidiano go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Small estate on the Ziros plateau above Sitia in the east, known for traditional Liatiko reds released many years after the vintage.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the flagship's exact label (Liatiko, or the Sitia PDO red of Liatiko and Mandilari) and its release habit from two sources; Thrapsathiri Odyssey goes in others if confirmed. The house is also written Oikonomou. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Heraklion house that helped carry Vidiano and Kotsifali onto export lists; its Vidiano is the grape as export lists meet it.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the founding year, the village, and the label's form and appellation from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Estate near Chania in the west of the island, known for its Nostos wines of Rhône grapes and for the local red Romeiko; the Nostos Roussanne is a Rhône white grown on Crete.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. IN DOUBT: no search confirmed the house or its wines this run. Confirm the house, its village, its founding year and the flagship (Nostos Roussanne, the Nostos red blend or the Romeiko) from two sources, or swap the pick. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: One of the island's first modern estates, near Argostoli, whose Robola helped restore Kefalonia's name abroad; the Cellar Selection, wild fermented and drawn mostly from the high Fagias vineyard, is its Robola of Cephalonia.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. The founding is given as 1984 in one source: confirm from two or leave it empty. Confirm the label form (Cellar Selection Wild Ferment), the vineyard, its altitude and the PDO; Wild Paths goes in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Family estate at Lixouri on the Paliki peninsula, farmed biodynamically; Vino di Sasso, the wine of stone, is its Robola, ripe and layered.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the biodynamic certification and its year, the PDO on the label and the founding year; Vostilidi and Mavrodaphne go in others. Name no living member of the family.

picks.why: The Robola co-operative of the Omala valley, founded by the growers of Omala and the villages around it in 1982 by one account, the year of the PDO, and later renamed; its Robola of Cephalonia is the island's bottling a server meets most often.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1982 for the co-operative and the PDO from two sources and the house's full name (the Robola Cooperative of Kefalonia); San Gerasimo, the high vineyard bottling, goes in others. Shares and volumes stay out.

picks.why: Family estate on the Paliki peninsula, one of the island's newer houses, reviving Vostilidi and other rare local grapes as dry wines beside its Robola.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the flagship (Vostilidi, or the house's Robola of Cephalonia) and its label, the village and the founding year from two sources; name no living member of the family.

picks.why: Winery among the fir trees of the Mount Ainos National Park, whose Robola comes from vineyards high on the mountain.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. IN DOUBT: the flagship was seen only in a tasting list. Confirm the house, its founding and the exact label (a Natural Robola is listed) and its PDO, or swap the pick. Name no living founder.

picks.producer: Union of Winemaking Cooperatives of Samos
picks.why: The growers' union founded in 1934 that makes most of the island's wine from small grain White Muscat; Samos Vin Doux, Muscat fortified with grape spirit, is the bottle any server meets.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 1934, the category the Vin Doux carries under the PDO, and the end of the union's exclusive rights (2016 by one source) from two sources; Nectar, of sun dried grapes, and Anthemis, aged in oak, go in others. Shares and volumes stay out.

picks.why: Family winery with roots in a Maltese family that settled on the island in the nineteenth century, among the first private wineries of Samos by one account; Nopera Vintage is its sweet Muscat of sun dried grapes.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm the house's founding, its village (Karlovasi is given) and that Nopera Vintage carries PDO Samos; Roya, a dry Muscat of PGI, and Epitome go in others. The first private winery is one source's claim: hedge it or leave it out. Name no living founder.

picks.why: Karlovasi winery founded in 2011 to make small lots, known for reviving Black Muscat; Epogdoon, its Samos of partly sun dried White Muscat, is the island's sweet wine from a private house.
picks.note: Not in WINE_PRODUCERS. Confirm 2011 and what the house bottled before private wineries could bottle the PDO, that Epogdoon carries PDO Samos, and the meaning of its name from two sources; Kalypso and Filion go in others. Name no living member of the family.
